reason: Narrower: a bract on the scape, the leafless peduncle (the previous review mapped scape to peduncle PO_0009053), which is part of the inflorescence; mostly Bromeliaceae.

label: pseudoparaphyllium
parent: is_a PO_0005679 (plant epidermis, as for paraphyllium PO_0030069); part_of PO_0030020 (gametophore axis)
definition: A small leaf-like, scale-like or filamentous outgrowth of a moss gametophore axis that is found only around a branch primordium or at the base of a branch, not scattered between the leaves.
reason: Pleurocarpous moss character used in 4 floras (foliose/filamentous/lanceolate/absent). It differs from paraphyllium (PO_0030069), which grows between the leaves along the stem, so it is not a synonym. Propose upstream to PO next to paraphyllium.
Narrower: the segments of the epicalyx ('epicalyx lobes 4', 'lanceolate', 'connate') are its bracts, free or joined at the base; PO_0025577 is the unit that floras count.
The unit a count is given per ('spines 30-51 per areole'), not a bearer; same as 'per node' and 'per side' in the previous review. The counted part (spine, sorus) is the bearer.

Fern indumentum scales on the stipe. The reviewed sense split for 'scale' sends indumentum scales to trichome, and stipe was mapped to stalk; express as trichome with the stipe as its whole (pattern 12 / part-of).

Narrower: the outer ring of a double peristome; PO defines peristome as a single or double circle of teeth. 'Exostome teeth' fits peristome tooth (PO_0030043). Exostome and endostome could be proposed to PO later.

Narrower: the slender thread-like divisions between the endostome segments, i.e. lobes of the inner peristome (PO: a peristome tooth is a single lobe of a peristome). Counted and described as 'nodose', 'rudimentary'.
Narrower: a moss tuber is a multicellular asexual propagule (gemma) borne on the rhizoids. It is not the vascular-plant tuber (PO_0025522).
Narrower: the scale-like nectaries at the base of the carpels (Crassulaceae) and similar flower nectaries.
Narrower: a flower nectary shaped as a ring or cushion round the ovary ('annular', 'raised on ovary apex').
Exact: the leaves that surround the archegonia; perichaetial/perichaetal are spelling variants.

label: perianth tube
parent: is_a PO_0025001 (cardinal organ part); part_of PO_0009058 (perianth)
definition: The tubular basal part of a perianth whose tepals are fused, below the free perianth lobes.
reason: No PO class. Matches the FLOPO local classes corolla tube (FLOPO_0985018) and perianth lobe (FLOPO_0986004); used by 4 floras (Iridaceae, Amaryllidaceae, Thymelaeaceae, etc.). Not the hypanthium (PO_0009065), which also carries the stamens and is not formed from the tepals alone. Propose upstream to PO together with corolla tube.

Narrower: a gland at the base of an organ (leaf blade, petiole, anther). Mapped the same way as gland and as 'basal vein' to leaf lamina vein in the previous review; the position is not a separate class.
'2-3-stratose' gives the number of cell layers of the lamina or margin. It is a quality (count or thickness) of that part, not a part.
Narrower: the network of tertiary and higher-order veins. Mapped like veinlet in the previous review, to the parent leaf lamina vein.
PO already lists verticillaster as a synonym of cyme inflorescence: a false whorl made of a pair of opposite cymes (Lamiaceae). Likely a plural/lexicon gap.
Narrower: a division of a branched stigma (counted 2-5, papillose).
The tunic is the dry, papery or leathery outer scale leaves (or leaf bases) of a bulb. Express as scale leaf with bulb as the whole.
Narrower: a dormant overwintering bud of woody plants ('glutinous', 'shiny') and the turion of aquatics. Bud covers both; PO lists turion only as a BROAD synonym of shoot systems.
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to (leaf, lip, corolla), like 'lateral lobe' in the previous review.
A cell of the stem cortex (mosses including Sphagnum, Characeae-like descriptions); express as cell with cortex as its whole. The cortex itself is not a new term.

Narrower: in these examples it is the network of higher-order leaf veins ('prominent above', 'areolate'). In other contexts it can mean surface sculpture of a seed or pollen grain, so use it only where the subject is a leaf.
Narrower: a division of a branched style (Asteraceae, Iridaceae, Euphorbiaceae); counted and shaped.

Calymperaceae: the region of large hyaline cells in the moss leaf base (leaf base has the synonym phyllid base). The qualities (broad, truncate, acute distally) describe that region. Family-specific, so I map it as a region rather than adding a new class.

label: lignotuber
definition: A woody swelling at the base of the stem, at or below the ground, that holds dormant buds and food reserves from which the plant resprouts after fire or cutting.
reason: Presence or absence is a diagnostic character in several floras (Arctostaphylos, Eucalyptus); there is no PO class. The French width/thickness examples may be trunk burls (abnormal wood swellings) and need checking. Propose upstream to PO.
Narrower: the shorter veins between the main lateral veins (intersecondaries). They are not secondary leaf veins in the strict sense, so map to the parent leaf lamina vein.
Moss character: the large thin-walled cells in a row across the costa. Express as cell with costa as its whole; counted 2-4.
Narrower: a canal in the leaf that holds resin or latex (Clusiaceae, Anacardiaceae), often seen as black lines. Use resin canal (PO_0005665) only where the secretion is stated to be resin.
Narrower (collective): PO's comment on alar cell says the area they form is 'sometimes called the alar region'; its size, shape and colour are qualities of the group of alar cells.
A quality-word fragment of 'pairs of free pinnules/leaflets'. The counted part is the noun that follows, and 'free' is its quality.
